# Janua Full LLM Context

Generated: 2026-05-13 · contracts section updated 2026-09-07

## Purpose

This file gives LLM agents a stable, tool-agnostic map for working in this
repository without depending on vendor-specific instruction files.

## Canonical instruction order

1. `AGENTS.md`
2. `README.md` if present
3. `ECOSYSTEM.md` if present
4. Relevant files under `docs/`, `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, and source
   directories for the specific task

## Agent compatibility

`AGENTS.md` is the source of truth. `CLAUDE.md` exists only to redirect Claude
and other legacy agent integrations to `AGENTS.md`.

## Enclii-first operations contract

Use Enclii web, API, or CLI for routine production provisioning, deployment,
observability, domain management, secrets, provider operations, scaling,
rollback, and remediation.

Raw `kubectl`, `helm`, SSH, provider CLIs/APIs, `docker exec`, and direct
container access are allowed only for platform bootstrap or documented
break-glass emergencies when Enclii is unavailable or lacks an implemented
adapter. Any break-glass use must record the actor, reason, target
service/environment, commands executed, result, and follow-up Enclii adapter
gap or incident link.

## Durable contracts an agent must not break

These are load-bearing behaviours with production evidence behind them. Changing
one is a decision, not a refactor. Each names the file that owns it.

### Sending identity — `app/services/sender_binding.py`, `email_sender.py`

A From header pairing a client's display NAME with an address on MADFAM's domain
(`Crea Tu Mundo <hola@madfam.io>`) must never be produced. Display name and
address move together on one fact: is the binding's address domain verified for
the ACCOUNT that will send it. There is no intermediate state. This reversed an
earlier rule after the forbidden header reached a real client inbox on
2026-09-07; several tests exist only to assert it can never recur, so a test
naming that string is a guard, not a stale reference.

Verification is per ACCOUNT, not per domain. A tenant on its own provider
account reads its own `verified_domains`; the global `RESEND_VERIFIED_DOMAINS`
describes MADFAM's account only.

A missing tenant credential degrades the sender to the platform From line and
logs `sender_credentials.tenant_credential_missing`. It never blocks the send: a
degraded From is a degraded outcome, a magic link that never arrives is an
outage.

`credential_ref` names an ENV VAR for CTM, not a Vault path, because janua-api
runs with no `VAULT_ADDR`/`VAULT_TOKEN` — a `path#field` reference cannot
resolve at runtime in production. Vault reaches the pod through an
enclii-managed ExternalSecret instead.

### Magic links — `app/auth/hosted_hop.py`, `routers/v1/auth.py`

`GET` on the magic-link callback spends nothing; only `POST` exchanges. Mail
scanners GET every URL in an email, and this estate has already lost a live
ceremony to a scanner-consumed link.

When the destination host cannot receive the estate cookie (it is outside
`COOKIE_DOMAIN`), the link lands on janua for one hop and then forwards
`?token=<access_token>` to the registered `redirect_url`. The rule is DERIVED
from the cookie domain, never configured, so it cannot drift from the relay
guard in `@madfam/janua-next`. Products land the forward with 0.3.0 or later.

### Estate session — `app/auth/sso_cookie.py`

`janua_sso` is HttpOnly, `Domain=.madfam.io`, and outranks `janua_access_token`
at `/authorize`. It is the only session that reaches the browser across the
estate, because products exchange magic links server-to-server and Node drops
the `Set-Cookie` on a fetch response.

## Email API surface — `apps/api/app/routers/v1/email.py`

Two internal send endpoints under `/api/v1/internal/email/`:

- `POST /send` — raw email: caller supplies `html`/`text`, subject, recipients.
- `POST /send-template` — renders a registry template with `variables`.

Also `GET /templates` (lists the registry live) and `GET /health` (reports
`templates_available` as `len(EMAIL_TEMPLATES)`, a live count).

The template registry is two paired dicts in the same file: `EMAIL_TEMPLATES`
(id → description, `required`/`optional` variables, `subject`, optional
`default_from_email`) and `TEMPLATE_FILENAMES` (id → whitelisted HTML filename
under `templates/emails/`). An id must be in both. A template with no HTML file
falls back to `generate_fallback_html()` rather than erroring.

**Two render paths — do not conflate them.** The `send-template` route renders
with **naive `{{key}}` string substitution** (`render_template()`): no Jinja
conditionals, loops, or auto-escaping. Anything conditional is composed in
Python first (e.g. `map/pago-confirmado` derives `{{sesiones_detalle}}` from an
optional count in `_derive_template_variables()`). The **Jinja2** path
(`FileSystemLoader`, autoescape) lives in `services/email_i18n.py` and
`services/email/resend_service.py` and renders the localized auth/magic-link
mail via `email_service.py` — a different template set, not this route.

**Sender resolution** is not the caller's to dictate: the From line is chosen by
`services/email_sender.py` under `EMAIL_SENDER_POLICY.md` (THE RULE above). A
caller's explicit `from_email` is honoured only from a verified domain; a
template may declare a `default_from_email` (e.g. `billing/cfdi` →
`facturacion@madfam.io`); otherwise the sender resolves from `org_id` or the
`redirect_url` host (e.g. `map/pago-confirmado` → Crea Tu Mundo). `attachments`
on either endpoint are forwarded to Resend (used for CFDI XML+PDF delivery).

Full walkthrough and the template table: `docs/MADFAM_EMAIL_INTEGRATION.md`.
